name: The Grotto

facts.claim: The Grotto frames the coastline through a natural window of rock on the Shipwreck Coast
It sits just beyond Port Campbell, near London Bridge and The Arch, off London Bridge Rd
The three stops offer lookouts, sea caves and arches shaped by limestone, wind and waves

name: Bay of Islands

facts.claim: Bay of Islands Coastal Park has ocean-carved cliffs, secluded rock stacks and sheltered bays near Peterborough
It is quieter than nearby big-name Great Ocean Road stops, about 400 km from Melbourne along the road
Sea kayaks can launch from Boat Bay Road at Bay of Islands beach; cliff-top heathland walks have sea views
Southern right whales can be seen off the coast between May and October

facts.claim: Port Campbell is a town on the Great Ocean Road, west of the Twelve Apostles, in the Shire of Corangamite
Whales are often spotted from lookouts along the coast, including Port Campbell township, during migration season
It is the base for the Shipwreck Coast sights

name: Flagstaff Hill Maritime Museum

facts.claim: Flagstaff Hill Maritime Village is in Warrnambool, on Victoria's south-western coast
The museum is built on Flagstaff Hill, which also holds the original lighthouses and Warrnambool Garrison
A sound and light show, Tales of the Shipwreck Coast, runs at dusk (listed on operator booking page)

name: Deep Blue Hot Springs

facts.claim: Deep Blue Hot Springs is a geothermal bathing sanctuary at Worm Bay Road, Warrnambool
It has indoor bath house and outdoor bathing pools; sessions are about two hours
Daytime entry is for ages five and up; evening sessions are adults 16 and over

name: Tower Hill

facts.claim: Tower Hill Wildlife Reserve sits in a large volcanic crater, a dormant volcano near the Great Ocean Road
Emus, kangaroos, koalas, swans and ducks live in the reserve
Walks range from easy boardwalks to the Tower Hill Peak Walk, with the Lava Tongue and Wagon Bay Loop walks
About 15 km north-west of Warrnambool
